claims.text: The baseline material is equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
As-cast equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi is single-phase FCC.
The as-cast alloy has a homogeneous chemical composition.
The as-cast alloy lacks pronounced chemical short-range ordering.
Annealing at 400–600 °C for approximately 2 hours followed by rapid cooling induces nanoscale compositional ordering in CoCrFeMnNi.
Annealing-induced short-range ordering produces nanoscale compositional fluctuations.
The nanoscale compositional fluctuations form magnetic clusters within the FCC matrix.
The induced magnetic clusters locally enhance exchange interactions.
Enhanced local exchange interactions reduce the energy barrier for magnetic-domain reorientation at low applied fields.
Reduced barriers to domain reorientation produce a greater low-field isothermal entropy change.
Annealed specimens will have a higher isothermal entropy change under fields up to approximately 1 T than the as-cast baseline.
Annealed specimens will exhibit less magnetization hysteresis than the as-cast baseline.
A continuous conductive FCC matrix enables rapid heat exchange.
Controlled annealing and nanoscale ordering will not compromise mechanical integrity relative to the as-cast state.
Annealing outside 400–600 °C or for significantly longer times may cause uncontrolled ordering or phase transformations.
Excessive ordering or unwanted phase separation may increase hysteresis and degrade mechanical properties.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that phase transformations caused by out-of-range temperatures or substantially longer anneals fall outside the mechanism's domain, whereas the falsification rule treats unwanted phase transformation or excessive ordering as falsifying the hypothesis. An out-of-bound processing result would not by itself decisively falsify the bounded mechanism.
